rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child directive: it describes a national conference concerning children and youth, emphasizes that effective action must occur in States and communities, and calls for State-level bodies to participate through conferences developed from the national undertaking. The child compresses and adapts that same conference-to-State-participation machinery for the Midcentury White House Conference. C15 is related through Oscar R. Ewing, child welfare, and State cooperation, but lacks the distinctive national-conference and State-conference structure. C03 contains a generic appeal to Federal, State, and local participation in youth-related observances and is weaker still.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I HAVE called a Midcentury White House Conference on Children and Youth
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a National Conference on Prevention and Control of Juvenile Delinquency
shared_material.explanation: Both establish or invoke a presidentially supported national conference focused on children and youth.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The value of this conference will depend upon full participation of each state.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the holding of State and community conferences, developed on the general pattern of the national Conference
shared_material.explanation: Both make State-level participation an operative extension of the national conference.

shared_material.child_excerpt: either you designate an existing body broadly representative in your state, or appoint a state committee to serve for this conference
shared_material.parent_excerpt: many important agencies, governmental and private, national and local, and individuals the country over, banded together ... [and] urged upon the States and communities immediate action
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts the parent's broad, multilevel mobilization into a specific mechanism for representative State committees.
